The questions are answered based on the provided Bengali passages:

[id 24] The Rule of Thirds creates dynamism (B), places subjects in effective spots (C), and establishes a rhythm (D). Option A (creating a base line) is not explicitly mentioned as a defining part/goal in the text provided, though it's a common technique, the text focuses on lines and division. However, looking at the text: "creating rhythm/dynamism" (B/D) and "effective placement" (C) are all mentioned. A is not in the text.
[id 25] The text says many common formats (like APS) have aspect ratios *equal to or close to* 3:2. It does *not* state that 35mm has a *different* aspect ratio than others; rather, it says others are similar. Option C is the least accurate description of the relationship described.
[id 26] Option D says the emphasis on personal experience is *compared* to other religious beliefs, whereas the text says it is *distinguished/differentiated* (আলাদা করা যেতে পারে) from them.
[id 27] The text says it covers "some regions" of North-East Afghanistan, not "all regions" (সকল অঞ্চল).
[id 28] The text states "the cost of war... was paid by the Filipino people themselves" (ফিলিপিনো জনগণ নিজেরাই দিয়েছিল).
[id 29] The text mentions morphine, scopolamine, stopping bleeding/arteries, and dissecting to prevent decay/blood loss. It does *not* mention treating Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) with sleeping pills.
[id 30] The text states: "Vision... depends on sensory organs or eyes" (চোখের উপর দৃষ্টিশক্তি... নির্ভর করে).
[id 31] The text says Sikhs acknowledge Hindu roots but maintain their religion is different. It does not say the "core of rituals" (আচার অনুষ্ঠানের মূল) is Hinduism; it says the "Guru" is the center of the belief. Option D is an incorrect representation of the text's nuances.
